# CircuitPythonSync file copy manifest
# Lines starting with # are comments (ignored). Blank lines are ignored.
# Format:  source_file  or  source_file -> /destination_on_board


readme.txt

# CircuitPythonSync "easy switch mechanism"; insert following line:
# ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
#    `foo.py -> /code.py`
# which copies workspace `foo.py` onto the *board* as `code.py`. Local `code.py` is
# unchanged. When using this switch mechanism, comment out the `code.py` line first, 
# because two sources to the same destination is an error. Then run Copy Files to Board.
#
# IMPORTANT: never put a trailing inline comment after an ACTIVE `source -> /dest`
# line. Confirmed 2026-09-12: neither this experiment's own `scripts/sync_files_to_board.py`
# nor the CircuitPythonSync extension strips text after the destination path -- a line like
# `foo.py -> /code.py # some note` copies to a literal file named "code.py # some note"
# on the board instead of "/code.py", silently leaving the real /code.py stale. Put the
# description on its own comment line directly above the entry instead (see below).

# code.py
# Tier 1 sync, minimal (basic primitives + brightness floor)
# code_stage0.py -> /code.py
# Tier 1 sync, broader (patterns + arrows + rotations)
# code_stage1.py -> /code.py
# Tier 2 async display + rotate-mid-scroll (steps 1-12: adds rotate-while-scrolling)
code_stage2.py -> /code.py
